title: The 5 stages of a ransomware attack, and how to stop each
description: Ransomware rarely hits instantly. It moves through five stages, and every one is a chance to stop it before your files are locked.

scenes.say: Ransomware doesn't strike instantly. It usually moves through five stages, and each one is a chance to stop it.
One, get in, often through phishing or an exposed login. Two, spread and gain admin rights. Three, quietly copy data out. Four, encrypt files. Five, show the ransom demand.

scenes.caption: The warning signs
scenes.say: Stages two and three leave clues. New admin accounts, huge uploads, switched off backups. Spot those, and you may stop the attack before a single file is locked.
Prevent early with multi-factor authentication, patching and email filtering. Recover late with offline backups, and a network split into sections so attackers can't roam freely.

scenes.sub: an untested backup is just a hope
scenes.say: And test those backups. If they won't restore, they won't save you. See you in the next one.
